# Lance fixtures

Datasets that the `lance_fdw` regression suites read, plus the reference output
they are checked against. Everything here is produced by pylance on the host —
nothing is hand-written.

```
gen_fixtures.py     generator: writes data/, expected/*.jsonl and manifest.json
upload_minio.py     syncs data/ into the MinIO bucket used by the s3:// cases
manifest.json       what each dataset contains (committed, reviewable)
expected/<name>.jsonl   one JSON object per row, read back with pylance (committed)
data/<name>.lance/  the datasets themselves (gitignored, regenerated)
```

```sh
make gen                      # regenerate everything except 'big'
make gen GEN_FLAGS=--with-big # ... including the AC5 timing dataset
make upload                   # push data/ to s3://$LANCE_S3_BUCKET/fixtures/
make test                     # pytest; generates data/ first if it is missing
```

`make test` and `.venv/bin/python -m pytest test/fixtures -q` are the same
thing. The tests regenerate the fixtures into a temporary directory and compare
byte for byte, so a generator change that would invalidate the committed
reference fails there.

## Datasets

| name | rows | fragments | what it is for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `types_all` | 24 | 3 | Every A-tier Arrow type of DESIGN §2, NULLs in every column. The per-column NULL pattern has period 7, so with 8 rows per fragment and `batch_size=3` the NULLs land at different in-batch offsets in every batch. AC3/AC4's main fixture. |
| `types_b` | 12 | 2 | B-tier columns (struct, dictionary, uint64, `list<list<int64>>`, `list<struct>`, duration) beside two A-tier ones, so `IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA` has something left after skipping them (AC2), and a hand-written foreign table can reference a B-tier column to get the AC4 error. |
| `deleted` | 16 | 4 | Rows 0, 3, 11 and 19 deleted, leaving deletion files on fragments 0, 2 and 3 and none on fragment 1. Deleted rows must not appear (I9), and the resulting sliced batches have non-zero `array->offset`. |
| `empty` | 0 | 0 | Schema, no data. pylance writes no fragment at all, so every QE gets an empty share. |
| `frag_1` … `frag_100` | 5 … 100 | 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 | Fragment-count coverage for the 3-segment modulo split (AC5): fewer fragments than segments, exactly as many, and far more. All fragments are the same size, so per-segment row counts are predictable. `frag_100` holds one row per fragment to keep the reference file small. |
| `frag_gap` | 15 | 3 | Fragment 1 deleted whole. Surviving fragment ids are 0, 2, 3 — nothing may assume ids are dense or start at 0. |
| `evolved` | 20 | 4 | Two `add_columns` calls (`v10 = id * 10`, `vup = upper(v)`), so each fragment's columns live in three data files. |
| `blob` | 4 | 2 | MiB-sized payloads twice: a plain `large_binary` column and one carrying Lance's `lance-encoding: blob` field metadata. Values are 1 MiB, empty, NULL and 2 MiB. |
| `large_text` | 8 | 2 | `large_utf8` from empty to 1 MiB, including `漢字`-repeats where byte length and character length differ, next to a short `utf8` column. |
| `versions` | 35 | 3 | Three versions of 10, 20 and 35 rows, append-only, for version pinning (AC6). |
| `big` | opt-in | 3 | AC5 wall-time comparison only: `--with-big` writes 3 fragments of 512 rows × 1 MiB. Random payloads, no expected output, not regenerated byte for byte. |

Every dataset's first column is a non-null `id` that ascends across fragments,
and `expected/<name>.jsonl` is in that order, so SQL cases compare against it
with `ORDER BY id`.

`manifest.json` records, per dataset: row count, fragment ids and their row
counts (before and after deletions), which fragments carry a deletion file, how
many data files each fragment has, the version history with row counts, and the
Lance file format version — plus, per column, the Arrow type, the Arrow C data
interface format string that lance-c and nanoarrow will see, the DESIGN §2 tier
and the PG type an A-tier column should import as.

## Expected output format

One JSON object per line, keys in schema order, ASCII-escaped:

| Arrow type | spelling |
|---|---|
| NULL (any type) | `null` |
| bool | `true` / `false` |
| all integers | JSON number |
| float16/32/64 | JSON number with Python's shortest round-trip repr; `"NaN"`, `"Infinity"`, `"-Infinity"` as strings, because JSON has no literals for them |
| decimal128(p,s) | string, never scientific notation, scale preserved (`"0.0000000000"`) |
| date32 | `"YYYY-MM-DD"` |
| timestamp | ISO-8601 with exactly as many fractional digits as the Arrow unit; tz-aware values are converted to UTC and suffixed `Z`, naive values carry no suffix |
| utf8 / large_utf8 | JSON string |
| binary / large_binary | lowercase hex string |
| fixed_size_list / list | JSON array of encoded elements |
| B-tier columns | best-effort JSON; the FDW never reads these |

A string or binary column whose longest value exceeds
`digest_threshold_bytes` (4096) is written as `{"chars", "bytes", "md5"}` /
`{"bytes", "md5"}` instead of the literal value — that is `blob.plain_lb`,
`blob.blob` and `large_text.txt`. SQL compares those with `octet_length()`,
`length()` and `md5()`; every other column is compared literally. Which
encoding a column got is recorded in `manifest.json` as `expected_encoding`.

## Things pylance 11.0.0 decided for us

Recorded here because they shape what the later packages can test. The file
format each dataset was written in is in `manifest.json`
(`data_storage_version`, `file_format_versions`); pass
`--data-storage-version 2.0` to the generator if lance-c turns out not to read
2.1 (DESIGN Q4).

- **No `map` column.** WORKPLAN §2.0 asks for one in `types_b`, but pylance 11
  refuses to write Arrow `map` into either Lance file format: *"Map data type is
  not enabled by the selected file format"* (2.1) and *"Lance v2.0 has no field
  encoding for 'c' with data type Map"* (2.0). The other B-tier dimensions are
  all there. Arrow `month_day_nano_interval` is rejected too
  (*"Unsupported data type: Interval(MonthDayNano)"*), so duration stands in for
  the interval/duration row of the B-tier list.
- **No zero-row fragment.** Deleting every row of a fragment makes Lance drop
  the fragment, and `LanceFragment.create()` rejects empty input, so `frag_gap`
  can only offer a hole in the fragment id sequence. The "a QE gets no rows"
  case is covered by `empty` and by `frag_1`/`frag_2` on three segments.
- **Blobs come back inlined.** Reading the `lance-encoding: blob` column with
  `to_table()` returns the bytes, not a position/size descriptor — that is
  DESIGN Q3 answered from the Python side only; what lance-c's scanner returns
  is still T2's question.
- **`pa.string()` stays `utf8` and `pa.large_string()` stays `large_utf8`**
  through a write/read round trip (DESIGN Q5), as do `binary`/`large_binary`,
  `float16`, `decimal128`, `fixed_size_list` and timestamp zone names.
- **Timestamps in `types_all` are microsecond-aligned on purpose.** PG stores
  microseconds, so an A-tier read of a nanosecond column must be exact; a value
  with sub-microsecond digits would have to be an I7 error instead, which is a
  different test than AC3's "equals pylance".
